| [ADR-050](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-050.md) v2 | A claim that calls something organized, a perspective, an agent, effective, exhausted, constituted or grounded says which sense, target or criterion it means | The perspective line's conclusions turn on distinctions the prose keeps locally and the vocabulary does not enforce: structure against efficacy, efficacy against competence and legitimacy, explanatory sufficiency against constitution, a perspective against an agent. A proposal the owner relayed on 2026-10-22 asked for a small grammar of these words, not a term for each. The decision, Proposed, is a usage protocol: each flagged word in a claim, question, term or reading must name its sense, target or criterion where it carries a substantive inference, though not in unambiguous ordinary uses. Two words get terms of their own (organization, [TERM-074](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-074.md); perspective, [TERM-072](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-072.md)); the rest are handled here.
